reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that win probability in NCAA tournaments can be modeled using a probit function of seeding rank differences. The authors extend earlier work by Boulier-Stekler, incorporating consensus rankings derived from multiple sources to improve prediction accuracy. The probit model assumes a linear relationship between transformed predictors (seed differences) and log-odds of victory. This formulation allows for probabilistic forecasts across all tournament rounds. The key innovation lies in applying ensemble methods (consensus rankings) alongside traditional seeding, leveraging the principle that collective estimates outperform individual ones—a concept rooted in macroeconomic forecasting theory. Each primitive operates within distinct regimes: seed rank difference provides baseline discrimination, consensus ranking enhances robustness, and the probit model synthesizes both into actionable probability estimates. Failure modes occur when extreme upsets deviate from expected patterns or when consensus data becomes too noisy.
